At establishment there is no earlier beat and nothing is already installed, so both sentences read as instructions to emit nothing, on the one stage whose entire job is to state what already stands. The JA pack had adapted exactly these two sentences ('開幕の場面がそうした機材を備えているなら、ここで設置する' / '機材がなければ何も出さない') and EN had not; EN now says the same thing, and both packs gain the reason -- there is no earlier beat for a channel to have been installed in, so one not declared here is not there when play begins. `tests/test_director_comms_channel.py` derives that chunk's closing sentence and asserts it does not appear in either pack's establish sheet, so the next unadapted paste is caught in whichever pack it lands in. Measured on the resolve side the same week and recorded under `prompts.director_interpret` in this ledger: a field present in the schema, the payload and the sheet's prose but not in the shape drew ZERO emissions, correctly, because as far as the model could tell the field did not exist. Both packs gain the same shape entry, carrying the id and the `duplex`/`broadcast` vocabulary the applier already owns. ROOM-SIZE VOCABULARY CORRECTED 2026-09-01. The shape line published size:'small'|'medium'|'large'. world/spatial_geometry.ROOM_SIZES is six ordered values -- tiny, small, medium, large, huge, vast -- and `effective_room_size` reads a room's word against exactly that tuple and discards anything outside it. So three of the six were unreachable from the hand that sizes every room in the scene at beat zero, and the prompt did not merely omit them: by naming three of six as though they were the set, it told the model the other three do not exist. The two ends are the ones that carry information -- `tiny` and `vast` are what separate a cupboard from a cathedral, and both graded as their neighbours. The parenthetical was replaced rather than extended, because "'large' only when people can genuinely be across it" describes a three-value scale and is wrong on a six-value one; what replaces it states what the rank IS (how much floor there is to cross) and what reads it (proximity_rel's near/across judgement), plus the miss direction -- a word outside the six grades exactly as a room nobody sized, silently. Wording is deliberately the same class statement the spatial specialist's rooms chunk already carries, so the three hands that write `size` are taught one rule rather than three. Both packs carry the six tokens verbatim. This is a closed set the ENGINE owns and enumerates, which CLAUDE.md's no-word-lists rule explicitly exempts ("A closed set the engine OWNS and can enumerate is a schema; a list that tries to anticipate how English will phrase something is the thing that fails"). No word list was added here: the reader accepts these members and nothing else, so the enumeration can be finished, and the failure being fixed is that it was never shown in full to the hand that has to write it.
